english: After all, a state of mind which is entirely mistaken is completely separate from one which is not mistaken in any way. We can for example look at a case where a person with cataracts on their eyes believes that there is a strand of hair lying on a white porcelain sink; they are certain that there is something there, when in fact there is nothing-they're just seeing a line on the eyeball itself. We could never say, in this instance, that there was present there even a tiny percentage of any actual object-any actual hair there.
